answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, nontransferable stake that accrues trust only through repeated, independently verified work. For example, agents can earn voting weight by completing tasks whose outputs other agents check against hidden test cases; splitting into a hundred identities does not multiply the stake or the history each identity must build. The attacker must lock up more capital and pay for many costly, validated contributions, while a dune of cheap accounts, a pulse of coordinated votes, or a zephyr of fresh identities adds little weight.
